paper_metadata.title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Algorithms for Loan Collection Optimization with Loan Loss Provisions

summary: The paper presents a hybrid gate-based QAOA workflow for loan collection optimization on a 600-loanee, 5-action problem, using up to 35 qubits on a classical computer. It reports an empirical improvement of about 70% in expected net profit over a standalone classical GPR baseline for roughly 30–100 DPO actions, while reducing total provision from about 5.4 to 4.4 (18.5%).

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical loan collection optimization using divide-and-conquer grouping, QAOA on each subgroup, and classical greedy provision reduction; evaluated on a real Kasikornbank loan dataset and a simulated dataset.

algorithm.variant: QAOA within a hybrid divide-and-conquer + state reconstruction + greedy provision reduction pipeline
algorithm.ansatz: custom QAOA with problem Hamiltonian HA and ring-type mixer HB
algorithm.convergence_criteria: minimize Energy(θ)=⟨ψ|HB|ψ⟩ using COBYLA; run until θopt found (no explicit stopping threshold reported)
algorithm.parameter_initialization: randomized real numbers in [0,1) for θ

optimizer_settings.max_iterations: not explicitly reported; Appendix says maximum number of iterations η but value not given

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each loanee i is represented by M binary qubits x_{i,j}; action j is taken if qubit (i,j)=|1⟩. One action per loanee enforced by number-preserving mixer; DPO corresponds to j=1.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Local constraint ∑_{j=1}^{M} x_{i,j}=1 enforced by the mixer/initial state; LLP global constraint ∑_{i=1}^{N}∑_{j=1}^{M} l_{i,j}x_{i,j}≤L handled classically by Greedy Provision Reduction (soft constraint in practice)

problem_instance.description: Loan collection optimization for a personal loan product with 600 loanees and 5 possible collection actions per loanee; evaluated on a proprietary Kasikornbank dataset and a simulated benchmark dataset.

dataset_specification.description: 600 loanees; 5 actions per loanee; hi,j estimated from Q-learning on historical data; li,j from repayment/default, expenses, credit losses, economic conditions, interest rate and tax policy; Ai,i' from internal transactions

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Association matrix built from internal transactions; community detection via greedy modularity and Louvain; recursive edge-node augmentation; simulated dataset uses modified Benford-law sampling for h_{i,j} and Erdős-Rényi graph for A_{i,i'}
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Numerical benchmarking comparing hybrid algorithm against standalone classical GPR; results shown for ϵ=0.5, varying ϵ, and varying number of DPO actions N_f; QAOA performed on a classical computer; no independent-run count reported

implementation_details.classical_solver: COBYLA for QAOA parameter optimization; classical greedy provision reduction; greedy modularity and Louvain community detection; Q-learning for estimating h_{i,j}
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Recursive division of the loanee network into subgraphs using greedy modularity and Louvain; edge-node introduction; state reconstruction from subgroup bitstrings
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Greedy Provision Reduction iteratively changes actions to reduce LLP while minimizing loss in Y

speedup_claims.conditions: for N_f approximately 30-100 DPO actions on the Kasikornbank dataset
speedup_claims.caveats: This is an empirical improvement in expected net profit, not an asymptotic computational speedup.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; only a 35-qubit classical simulation and a 600-loanee benchmark are reported.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: A gate-based QAOA implementation with up to 35 qubits, plus classical preprocessing/postprocessing (divide-and-conquer, COBYLA, GPR).
limiting_factors: No quantum hardware execution is reported
The reported improvement is empirical and against a classical GPR baseline only
Classical preprocessing and postprocessing dominate the workflow
Problem is solved on a classical computer with 35 logical qubits, so practical advantage is unverified

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_statevector because the paper states QAOA was performed using up to 35 qubits on a classical computer and no QPU/device is named.
Circuit depth not explicitly reported; only T=2 driving cycles is given, so depth is inferred to be related to the QAOA layer count but exact transpiled depth is unavailable.
Speedup order is not characterized asymptotically; the paper reports empirical improvement over a classical baseline only.

The authors claim the hybrid method improves expected net profit by about 70% over standalone classical GPR for N_f ≈ 30–100, but this is not a computational advantage claim and is not a demonstrated quantum speedup.
